justification: FAIL for HDFS-11896. Diagnosed a DIFFERENT phenomenon: the ~110TB absolute magnitude of CapacityUsedOther, attributed to a shared host filesystem across the ~50 containerized DataNodes each reporting the same non-service bytes (summed N x). That is a plausible real artifact of this Docker-compose cluster, but it is NOT the bug. The run never noticed the 172.25.0.38 dead->re-register event (log:107831/114118) nor the ~2.5TB jump across it (log:89776->121401), and never named resetBlocks() or the register() add-before-reset ordering. Anchored on the dominant benign explanation of the 'abnormally high' symptom and missed the target bug entirely.
claimed_root_cause: CapacityUsedOther inflated N x by shared-FS summing; Stats.add L409 unconditional; getOtherUsed returns stored not derived
gt_lines: DatanodeDescriptor.resetBlocks() L313-319 (omits setOtherUsed(0)) — THE root-causing line
HeartbeatManager.register() L189-196 (addDatanode/stats.add of stale otherUsed before updateHeartbeatState(EMPTY))
gt_branches: dead datanode 172.25.0.38 (log:107831) re-registers (log:114118) -> stale otherUsed re-added to capacityUsedOther -> +~2.5TB jump (109.85T@log:89776 -> 112.36T@log:121401)
